pairs.locus: Falco of Benevento, Chronicon Beneventanum, anno 1114.5 (Council of Ceperano)
pairs.question: Unde vis ut misericordiam super vobis habeamus?
pairs.answer: Domine, quia audivi vos erga me indignatos fore, cum me literis vestris arcessiri iussistis et curiam vestram non adveni.
pairs.derivation: At the Council of Ceperano Pope Paschal II questions Archbishop Landulph of Benevento. Question is the pope's words with the interleaved speech tag 'inquit' dropped (source: 'Apostolicus autem hoc audiens: "Unde vis", inquit, "ut misericordiam super vobis habeamus?"'). Answer is the archbishop's full single-sentence reply with its lead-in 'Et archipresul:' stripped; it directly states the ground on which he seeks mercy, answering 'unde vis'.

pairs.locus: Falco of Benevento, Chronicon Beneventanum, anno 1114.5 (Council of Ceperano)
pairs.question: Quare, ut ipse asseris, vocatus curiam non advenisti?
pairs.answer: Domine, pater, et timore coactus vestrae indignationis, et quorundam minantium, non adveni vocatus.
pairs.derivation: The pope follows up asking why the archbishop did not come when summoned. Question is the pope's words with speech tag 'inquit' dropped (source: 'Et Apostolicus: "Quare", inquit, "ut ipse asseris, vocatus curiam non advenisti?"'). Answer is the operative answering clause of the archbishop's reply with its lead-in 'Archiepiscopus ad haec: "Domine", inquit, "pater,' normalized (speech tag 'inquit' dropped); cut before 'et quod legatos meos episcopos quidem non accepisti...', which turns from answering the 'quare' to airing separate grievances about his envoys.

pairs.locus: Falco of Benevento, Chronicon Beneventanum, anno 1124.2 (miracle of Barbatus; vision of Ioannes Sutor)
pairs.question: Quare cum ceteris ad vigilias canandas coram ossibus preterito die non advenisti meis?
pairs.answer: Pater, quoniam dolore gravi brachium meum cum dextera tenebatur.
pairs.derivation: In Ioannes Sutor's reported dream, Saint Barbatus asks why he failed to come to the vigils. Question is Barbatus's words with the interleaved speech tag 'inquit' dropped (source: '"Quare", inquit, "cum ceteris ad vigilias canandas coram ossibus preterito die non advenisti meis?"'). Answer is the operative answering clause with its lead-in 'Et ego:' stripped; cut before 'sex etenim mensium spatio miser ego tali langore perturbor', which elaborates the affliction rather than answering 'quare'.

pairs.locus: Falco of Benevento, Chronicon Beneventanum, anno 1124.2 (miracle of Barbatus; vision of Ioannes Sutor)
pairs.question: Dicito mihi, quo nomine, pater, vocaris?
pairs.derivation: Ioannes asks the apparition his name. Question is the speaker's whole utterance with the narrative lead-in 'Addidi quoque:' stripped ('Dicito mihi' is the speaker's own words, retained). Answer is the apparition's reply with lead-in 'Et ille:' and the interleaved speech tag 'ait' dropped (source: '"Barbatus", ait, "Beneventanae quondam civitatis episcopus"').

pairs.locus: Falco of Benevento, Chronicon Beneventanum, anno 1124.3 (miracle of Barbatus; vision of the lame rustic)
pairs.question: Quis es qui mihi tantum thesauri pondus promittis?
pairs.derivation: After the apparition promises healing ('sanitatis gaudia... consequeris'), the lame rustic asks who he is. Question is the rustic's words with lead-in 'Et ille:' and interleaved speech tag 'inquit' dropped (source: 'Et ille: "Quis es", inquit, "qui mihi tantum thesauri pondus promittis?"'). Answer is the apparition's reply with the speech tag 'ait' dropped (source: '"Barbatus", ait, "Beneventanae civitatis episcopus"').
